title: Check out my game
author: lester36
selftext:
[https://rainbot.games/games/saintfall.html](https://rainbot.games/games/saintfall.html)

Check out my latest game Saintfall. The environment was made with opus 5. I used a combo of opus 5 and gpt 5.6 sol for ui and gameplay mechanics. I used meshy for player models and a couple objects in the environment but most of the assets are generated by opus. I used suno for music. 

Little background: I love playing with AI. I have no technical background but always loved the idea of making a game since I was a kid. I have been trying out ai for coding since gpt 4 but it wasn't until opus 4.6 when it felt much more approachable. Since then I have been making games and work/life related apps. I made the Rainbot site to host all the games I have made. My brother made a few as well. Saintfall took me about a month. I spent about a month on Mr Feast as well (mostly gpt5.5). The rest are pretty basic or unpolished games which took 1-3 days for each of those.

I love the idea of making money from this but I don't really see a realistic path and I'm burning through money. I have learned a lot and it is definitely time consuming to polish a game. I wanted to put this out there since I will probably be slowing down on the game development for now. It is very addicting but I can't sustain this forever. I'll probably keep a few $20 subs to keep messing around. 

I know it could use a lot more work but I'm pretty impressed with what AI can accomplish and how fast it has progressed. I could barely get it to make a decent website a year ago. Anyways, let me know what you guys think!

comments.author: Lucky_Pangolin_3760
comments.body: holy moly those 3D models look insane.

comments.author: guanzo91
comments.body: Looks really good man. How did you make the intro cinematics? Like the rocket crashing on the planet.

replies.author: lester36
replies.body: I just asked opus 5 to create an intro sequence with a drop pod. I used meshy to create a better looking pod. It took a few back and forth prompts to make it what I wanted.

comments.author: weodawg
comments.body:
How did opus 5 do the environment exactly? Did it create assets or use some that you downloaded or created elsewhere? And how did it place them/sculpt terrain in the way you wanted? 

Looks great!

replies.author: lester36
replies.body: Thanks! I used a variation of the famous prompt people were using with opus 5 to 1 shot games but I told it environment only because I wanted to curate the gameplay step by step. I used the game Journey as a side by side comparison for it to match quality wise. I had to make a few edits to make the layout better and polish things but it did a really good job on its first attempt.

comments.author: thomthetank
comments.body: When you say assets generated by Opus did you just feed it examples and it generated them in blender?

replies.author: lester36
replies.body: I can tell you the 3 players models, the statue, and the cross was created using gpt5.6 to generate the art and use meshy and blender because opus cant create images. The rest of the environment and bosses as well as vfx was created by opus in threejs code I believe. I did not direct it to use blender. It may have without me realizing it...
